content:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to counteract downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 65), model often overreacts and overshoots in next 3-5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/positive.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.1) mid-horizon, model frequently underestimates upward momentum; add 1-2% buffer to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is 5-10% below recent 18d average, adjust upward by 2-3% to align with recent trend.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment is volatile (±0.35 or more in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast volatility by 10-15% to avoid overfitting to noise.
- When sentiment is flat (avg < 0.05 and > -0.1), model often underperforms; add 0.5-1.5% to forecast to capture latent market resilience.
